# Getting Started {#welcome}

Everything you need for your first two weeks. Work through the checklist below in order — most items depend on the ones above them.

---

## Day 1 checklist {#checklist}

**Before anything else:**

- [ ] Meet with the PI for a lab orientation walkthrough
- [ ] Complete HMSC lab safety training (links sent by PI before start date)
- [ ] Get keycard access to your assigned lab spaces — contact the lab manager
- [ ] Read this guide in full

**Accounts to set up:**

- [ ] **OSU email** — your primary institutional address; check with the PI if not provisioned
- [ ] **GitHub** — create an account at [github.com](https://github.com) if you don't have one, then request an invitation to the [GurrLab GitHub org](https://github.com/GurrLab)
- [ ] **Discord** — join the lab server (link from PI); introduce yourself in `#introductions`
- [ ] **OSF** — create a free account at [osf.io](https://osf.io) for pre-registration and data archiving
- [ ] **HPC cluster** — request an account on the OSU HPC; see the [Computing chapter](#computing) for details
- [ ] **SciShield** — lab safety and training management; link from PI or lab manager
- [ ] **OSU intake form** — complete the lab intake form (link from PI)

**Week 1:**

- [ ] Schedule a recurring 1-on-1 meeting with the PI (bi-weekly minimum)
- [ ] Attend lab meeting and introduce yourself
- [ ] Set up your computing environment (see [Computing](#computing))
- [ ] Read the Code of Conduct and lab philosophy chapters of this guide

**Week 2:**

- [ ] Shadow a graduate student or FRA on a lab task
- [ ] Submit your first commit to a lab GitHub repository (see [Daily workflow](#daily-workflow))
- [ ] Complete the OSU required trainings (RCR, animal/human subjects if applicable)

## Email norms {#email}

Email is for external collaborators, formal communications, and anything that needs a paper trail. For day-to-day lab communication, use Discord.

- Use your OSU address for all institutional and research correspondence
- CC the PI on emails to collaborators about active projects unless otherwise agreed
- For urgent operational matters (organism emergency, equipment failure), use Discord `#urgent` and text the PI directly

---

## Discord {#discord}

Discord is the lab's hub for async communication. No expectation of instant replies — treat it like a thoughtful group chat, not a live chat room.

| Channel | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `#general` | Lab-wide announcements and discussion |
| `#introductions` | New member intros — post yours in week 1 |
| `#computing-help` | Bash, R, HPC, and GitHub questions |
| `#papers` | Share and discuss recent literature |
| `#urgent` | Time-sensitive lab issues only |
| `#off-topic` | Non-work conversation |

---

## Meetings {#meetings}

**Lab meeting** — Full group, bi-weekly. Everyone attends unless a scheduling conflict is communicated to the PI in advance. Format rotates: paper discussion, project updates, skill workshops, and invited speakers.

**1-on-1 with PI** — Bi-weekly minimum for all lab members; more frequent during critical project phases or early in your program. Come prepared with an agenda — your time and the PI's time are both finite.

**Journal club** — [Frequency TBD by current group]. Rotating leader; papers distributed ≥48 h in advance.

---

## Lab norms {#norms}

These aren't rules so much as the working agreements that let the lab function well:

- **Null results belong in the lab.** Share what didn't work internally — it saves others from repeating dead ends.
- **Document at time of collection.** A lab notebook entry written a week later is a reconstruction, not a record. Use a physical lab notebook or the lab's digital equivalent and keep it current.
- **Ask early, not late.** If you are stuck, confused, or behind — tell someone. The PI would far rather hear about a problem early than discover it at a deadline.
- **Clean up after yourself.** Shared bench space, cold rooms, and husbandry areas depend on everyone. Leave equipment cleaner than you found it and return shared items promptly.
- **Respect organism welfare.** Your husbandry schedule deserves diligence. Hatfield has a resident veterinarian who conducts unannounced welfare checks. Neglect of organisms in any shared space will not be tolerated.
